page.subtitle: Scan the cloned repo to surface house-rules — each backed by evidence you can turn into a Skill.

empty.title: No conventions extracted yet
empty.body: Scan the repo to surface house-rules — naming, error handling, structure — each backed by evidence you can turn into a Skill.

page.candidateCount: {count, plural, one {# candidate} other {# candidates}} · grounded against sampled files

noEvidence.title: Nothing survived the evidence gate
noEvidence.body: The model proposed rules, but none of them cited code that could be found in the files it was shown. Re-scan, or index the repo first so the scan sees more than the config files.

page.dropped: {count, plural, one {# candidate was dropped} other {# candidates were dropped}} — the cited code was not in the sampled files.
page.sampleCount: {count, plural, one {# file sampled} other {# files sampled}}

selection.accepted: {count, plural, =0 {No rules accepted of {total}} one {# rule accepted of {total}} other {# rules accepted of {total}}}
selection.createSkillDisabled: Accept at least one rule to build a skill from it.

createSkill.title: Create skill from conventions
createSkill.subtitle: Nothing is stored until you press Create. Every field below is editable first.
createSkill.mergedFrom: Merged from {rules, plural, one {# accepted rule} other {# accepted rules}} citing {files, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}.
createSkill.previewEmpty: Nothing is accepted any more, so there is no skill to build. Close this and accept at least one rule.

fields.name: Name
fields.descriptionHint: What an agent reads to decide the rule applies. Write it as an instruction — “Enforce X”, not “About X”.
fields.enabledHint: An extracted skill is your own, not an import, so it starts enabled — attach it to an agent and the next run carries it.
fields.bodyHint: Generated from the accepted rules and their evidence. Edit it freely — what you see here is what reaches the prompt.

createSkill.tokensTitle: Estimated from the character count — the exact count comes from the provider and shows up in the run trace.
createSkill.splitHint: One skill per category instead of a single merged skill. Useful when you want to attach naming rules without the async ones.
createSkill.created: {count, plural, one {Created “{name}” — it is in the Skills Lab, ready to attach to an agent.} other {Created # skills — they are in the Skills Lab, ready to attach to an agent.}}
